#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name="rfm_PismTest1_pism_1_1_4__gcc__cijv4kn___nodes___1___mpi___64___omp___1__job"
#flux: -n 64
#flux: --ntasks-per-node=64
#flux: -c 1
#flux: -q c6gn
#flux: --exclusive

# The original script specified separate output and error files.
# Flux merges stderr with stdout by default when a single output file is specified.
#flux: -o rfm_PismTest1_pism_1_1_4__gcc__cijv4kn___nodes___1___mpi___64___omp___1__job.out

# The original script did not request a specific time limit, so none is added.

spack load pism@1.1.4 %gcc /cijv4kn
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OMP_PLACES=cores

# 'srun' is replaced by 'flux run'. It will launch the 64 tasks requested.
flux run /usr/bin/time -f "real:%e" pismv -test B -Mx 61 -Mz 11 -ys 422.45 -y 25000 &> pismv.out

reasons: Validation failed at directive: --ntasks-per-node=64. For a single-node job, it is more common and robust to specify the total number of tasks, e.g., '-n 64'.
issues: The script uses two different methods for output redirection: the `#flux: -o ...` directive and a shell redirection `&> pismv.out` on the `flux run` command. This will result in two separate output files; the `flux run` output will go to `pismv.out`, while the main job's stdout (if any other commands produced output) would go to the file specified in the directive. This is likely not the intended behavior and can make debugging difficult.

The use of `--exclusive` reserves an entire node. The job requests 64 tasks (`-n 64`) with 1 CPU each. If the node has more than 64 CPU cores, this will be an inefficient use of resources, leaving some cores idle.
